summary: Brick tower and keepers' duplex of 1872 at the mouth of St. Simons Sound, replacing a tabby tower of c.1810 that Confederates blew up in 1862.

Congress appropriated $7,000 on March 16, 1804 for a lighthouse on Saint Simons Island, and John Couper, owner of a plantation on the southern end of the island, sold four acres of his land to the government later that year for a token sum of one dollar.
The original appropriation reverted to the treasury in 1806, but Congress provided the much larger sum of $19,000 on March 3, 1807 for the project.

notes_for_editor: Conflicts: automation 1950 (LighthouseFriends), 1954 (our record), 1959 (NRHP update); USLHS roster ends 1950, LighthouseFriends gives O'Hagan to 1953. Osborne: USLHS says died 10 March 1880; the USCG Historian page (not readable, 403) reportedly says the shooting was 29 Feb 1880; no primary newspaper page was read (loc.gov search was queued behind other agents), so the Georgia Weekly Telegraph note is cited through a blog. Cause of the quarrel and the acquittal rest on LighthouseFriends and the blog. LighthouseFriends also lists Gus V. Dimick (1913) as assistant, absent from USLHS; omitted from the roster. The Peckham and Champagne first assistants share surnames with the head keepers; no source read says they were wives. 1896-97 Light-House Board volume has no page data, cited by volume. Oil-house year: NRHP possibly 1889, LF 1890, report in the 1891-92 volume (not certain which fiscal year). Record kind is range_lights; the 1895 front beacon is gone from the roster/NRHP detail. Tower height 104 ft per LighthouseFriends (record: 32 m). Lighthouse Board volume 1891-92 is cited without fiscal-year certainty.
